page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.d1.3xlarge is a storage-focused virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 12 dedicated vCPUs from an Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processor running at 2.5 GHz, paired with 48.0 GB of system memory. A defining characteristic of this instance is its massive local storage capacity, which bundles 35,433 GB of local HDD storage. The network interface provides a baseline bandwidth of 4 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate a clear division between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Single-core processing is weak, with stress-ng and Geekbench single-core scores falling into the bottom 10% to 25% categories. However, multi-core execution scales to average levels, as demonstrated by the Geekbench multi-core score of 4584.0 and Passmark CPU score of 10074.03. Memory performance is mixed; while cached read-only memory bandwidth reaches 488.85 GB/sec, the Passmark memory score is categorized as weak. Redis SET operations perform at an average rate of 8.27 million operations per second, while static web serving throughput is weak at 5.49 GB/sec.

From a resource density perspective, the ecs.d1.3xlarge offers high qualitative cost efficiency for applications requiring massive local storage capacity without needing high-speed solid-state drives. The primary tradeoff is the reliance on spinning HDDs and an older Intel Xeon architecture, which limits single-threaded compute performance and storage I/O operations per second compared to modern NVMe-based instances. This profile makes the instance appropriate for cold data storage, large-scale data archiving, log processing, and distributed file systems where storage volume is prioritized over raw compute speed.
